categories.summary: No new attacks on US bases, warships or tankers were found in the last day (checked today's attack headlines and a search). This week Iran hit a US radar site in Bahrain, fired drones at a US base in Kuwait (shot down), and a tanker was attacked in Hormuz. Reports that Trump is weighing new strikes remain unconfirmed. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no new warning signs.

sources.title: Cybernews: Visa confirms cyberattack as hackers claim JPMorgan hit too
Quartz: Hackers leak Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan data via vendors

categories.summary: The run of big overseas incidents continues but nothing new hit Australia today. New overseas: China-linked hackers used a hidden flaw in VMware server software for months before it was fixed (spying, now patched), and Expedia and chipmaker Nvidia face ransomware claims (criminal gangs, not confirmed). The collector says the 'China campaign' touches Australia, but that link comes from the card-data hack mislabelled as Australian; the hack was criminal and mostly US. Suspected Iran-linked attacks on fridges and small water systems stay in Europe and the US. Australian phones, banks and the grid are normal (the 'Telstra outage' headline is from July).

categories.summary: WHO reports Ebola in parts of Africa, MERS in Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and a pneumonia of unknown cause in Russia; none is spreading toward Australia. No Adelaide emergency departments are very busy.

categories.summary: Fire danger in the Mount Lofty Ranges is Moderate today and tomorrow, with no fire bans or CFS warnings near home. CFS put out two grass fires in the Hills today. headline: A quieter day: no new attacks on US bases or tankers were found, but the Strait of Hormuz stays shut, so fuel stays dear.
summary: No new attacks on US bases or tankers were found in the last day; this week's Iran-US exchanges in Bahrain, Kuwait and Hormuz are the latest. Hormuz is still effectively closed and oil eased again to about US$90, though share markets were jumpier (the US 'fear gauge' rose about 16%). The Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan data hack still shows no sign of affecting Australians. Near home, CFS handled two grass fires in the Hills today; fire danger in the Hills is only Moderate today and tomorrow.
